subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What aspects of their experience are Yelp reviewers talking about?

judge.implied_focus: Experiential aspects/dimensions of Yelp restaurant reviews (the review 'aspects' being discussed), organized around food and service experience

per_column.name: food_quality_rating
per_column.rationale: Captures the food-experience aspect and its sentiment valence, a core review dimension.

per_column.name: food_item_highlight
per_column.rationale: Adds granularity within the food aspect (specific dishes praised/criticized), a coherent facet.

per_column.name: service_quality_rating
per_column.rationale: Captures the service-experience aspect and valence, parallel to food_quality.

per_column.name: service_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Decomposes service problems into actionable subtypes, deepening the service facet.

per_column.name: staff_behavior_tone
per_column.rationale: Captures staff interpersonal tone, a distinct aspect of the service/staff experience.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on a single coherent, data-inferable focus: the experiential aspects of restaurant reviews. They cluster tightly around two well-formed dimensions -- food (quality valence + specific-item highlight) and service (quality valence + issue type + staff tone) -- rather than being a scattered grab-bag, and none are mechanical (no token counts or bare sentiment on the whole review). Structure is sound: each aspect has both a valence facet and a finer categorical facet, giving useful granularity beyond a single restatement, though there is mild overlap between service_issue_type and staff_behavior_tone (rude appears in both), and other plausible aspects (ambiance, price, wait time, cleanliness) are absent, slightly narrowing coverage of 'aspects of their experience.' The implied focus is clearly actionable -- an analyst could quantify which experiential dimensions dominate reviews and drill into specific failure modes. Deductions are for the narrow aspect coverage and the partial redundancy between the two service categoricals.
